text:
alex: Heads-up — ran into odd auth behavior when routing org-scoped keys through the edge proxy + project-impersonation. Some requests get 403 even though token has allowed_project claim.

maya: Can you paste a minimal repro / logs?

alex: Paste:
```
# curl to edge-proxy with org-scoped key
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://edge.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# token claims ->
{
  "sub": "sa:proj-123",
  "org": "org-77",
  "allowed_project": "proj-123",
  "iss": "auth.redwood.ai"
}
# response
{"error":"403","reason":"project_mismatch","route":"edge-proxy/fallback"}
```

alex: Notice route shows fallback path. If I hit dedicated backend directly, same token works.

ravi: This smells like the proxy normalization path that rewrites origin headers. @beth did we change claim propagation in the last deploy?

beth: We rolled a header-normalization change (2245) to canonicalize `x-origin` and `x-origin-project`. That change shouldn't strip JWT claims, only header names.

alex: I traced the middleware: when `x-origin-project` exists we validate it against routing table. On fallback the code path currently calls `validateAndDrop()` which accidentally drops the ephemeral `project` claim before we perform attribution. So attribution ends up empty -> project mismatch.

maya: Ugh. Do we have telemetry for claim vs attributed project? Would be nice to see how widespread mismatches are.

infra-bot: metric: auth.claim_mismatch.rate 3h: 0.02% -> 0.82% (prod-edge, last 3h)

ravi: Short-term fix: preserve the token claim or move validation after attribution. Long-term: surface claimed vs effective project in request traces and console request detail. Also add a per-key counter for mismatches.

beth: Agreed. For rollout we'll do a canary. Last time normalization touched EU traffic we saw an unrelated header issue.

kevin: I can own the console surface. Proposed UX: request detail shows two fields: "claimed project" and "effective project". Highlight mismatches in red + link to trace. Quick mock: small diff badge and a toggle to show raw claims.

alex: I'll open a tiny PR to guard the middleware (preserve claims on fallback + add unit tests). I'll include the log lines and a test that simulates proxy -> fallback path.

maya: Also add an opt-in telemetry flag on the canary so we can sample expanded traces (include raw claims) without running at 100%.

ravi: Deployment plan: canary 5% traffic for 30m, monitor auth.claim_mismatch.rate, request latency, and error budget. If stable, ramp to 25% then 100%.

alex: PR will reference the canary plan and include the test vectors. ETA for PR in ~2h.

beth: I'll create console backlog ticket and add Kevin.

kevin: I'll put together the mock and a tiny console ticket.

alex: Thanks — pinging infra to schedule canary window.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary window for 2026-03-21 02:00 UTC, 5% traffic. (will only start once PR merges)

maya: Nice, thanks. Once PR is up I'll add a short note to the incident slack if we see a spike during canary. :thumbsup:
